one_month_reasoning: Both in-window events are on 2026-10-15: the South32 AGM vote on selling its aluminium assets to Alcoa (12:00 AWST, before the US open; independent expert says fair and reasonable, board recommends unanimously, so very likely to pass and little price effect) and Alcoa's Q3 2026 results after the close (consensus ~$1.52 vs Q2 $2.12; the step-down is flagged by the July guidance of small sequential items and by sell-side target cuts). In round 1 I shaded the centre to $41.8 partly because I treated the Midwest premium as possibly back at 95c; the supervisor showed 95c was the 20 Aug Platts print and the CFO cited $1.09/lb on 10 Sep after the Canada tariff cut collapsed, so that negative input is weaker. LME is ~$3,250, well above bank decks, which supports Q3/Q4 realized prices. Peer chain (CENX) fell with AA in September, so the derating looks priced. No directional edge: centred at $42.0 with ~16.5% monthly sigma (56%/3.5 plus a bit for the earnings print).

P/E: normalized pro forma EPS $4.43 x 10x = $44.3 (w 0.45). Sell-side average target $63 (w 0.10). Blend ~$46.0.

FY2025 $1.965B at ~$2,630 LME; LTM $2.29B; ~+$0.2B per +$100/t LME on ~2.3Mt sold net of alumina cost linkage gives ~$2.5B at $2,900 before alumina weakness; alumina at ~$350-370/t FOB WA in widening surplus keeps the Alumina segment near breakeven (-$0.15B vs LTM).

Alcoa pays ~6.8x through-cycle for AliGroup, which caps the range; peer CENX derated from ~$70 to ~$36 in parallel, and the market values AA at ~3.5x run-rate. I keep 5.0x (supervisor uses 5.25x) because post-deal leverage (~1.0x normalized, higher if the deck fades) and an alumina-heavy mix deserve a discount to the deal multiple.

bear.story: Gulf smelters fully back by Q1 2027 and China at record output push LME to ~$2,500-2,600 (below GS's $2,700); the Canada tariff is cut after all and the Midwest premium falls toward $0.60/lb; alumina stays in surplus, hitting AliGroup's alumina-heavy assets. Combined EBITDA ~$2.2-2.4B, now carrying ~$5B of pro forma debt; 4.5x gives equity in the high $20s even after the Ma'aden credit.

base.story: LME ~$2,900, Midwest premium ~$0.95/lb with 50% tariffs intact; deal closes H1 2027; combined EBITDA ~$3.1B; stock re-rates to ~5x EBITDA / ~10x normalized EPS.

bull.story: Gulf restart slips or new disruption, tariffs persist (Section 232/338 escalation), Midwest premium stays >$1/lb and LME >$3,200; alumina recovers on Chinese cuts; combined EBITDA ~$4B plus synergies; deleveraging from strong FCF; stock moves toward sell-side highs.

thesis_break_reason: At $27 the pro forma equity (~282.8M shares) is ~$7.6B; with ~$3.1B of net claims at the horizon (after the Ma'aden credit and FCF) that is an EV of ~$10.7B, ~3.5x my $3.1B normalized combined EBITDA. That only makes sense if LME is heading to ~$2,500 with a collapsing Midwest premium, or if the AliGroup deal, its financing or WA bauxite approvals have gone wrong - a real downcycle rather than ordinary volatility. Lowered from $28 because the pro forma build (with the Ma'aden asset) gives more balance-sheet cushion per share than my round-1 standalone view implied, offset partly by higher leverage.

reasoning: Round 2 rebuild. The supervisor's main correction applies to me: I assumed the South32/AliGroup deal closes in 1H27 but valued standalone. Primary filings (8-K Ex.99.1/99.3, 2026-09-09; verified pro forma debt $5,420M and LTM EBITDA $3,154M vs $2,293M standalone) put the horizon company at ~$4.75B net debt, $0.57B pension, a $1.36B Ma'aden stake I had omitted, and 282.8M diluted shares. I also accept the Midwest premium correction ($1.09/lb on 10 Sep; 95c was a stale 20 Aug print) and that 9x on haircut EPS double-counted normalization. Rebuilt: combined EBITDA $3.1B (standalone $2.35B at ~$2,900 LME and ~$0.95/lb premium, AliGroup $0.75B trimmed for alumina surplus) x 5.0x less ~$3.07B net claims = $43.9; EPS $4.43 x 10x = $44.3; 10% weight on the ~$63 sell-side average; blend ~$46, the same as round 1 because the corrections largely offset (Ma'aden +, higher premium +, higher P/E +; deal per-share slightly dilutive at 5x, higher interest -). One point where I differ from the supervisor: it called Goldman's $2,700 2027 cut 'newest', but the Newsquawk headline is dated early July 2026, and LME has stayed ~$3,250 since, so I do not treat it as fresh negative information; I still put my deck below spot because EGA's full restart is due Q1 2027. I keep 5.0x rather than 5.25x for leverage and the alumina-heavy mix. Distribution: scenarios 27/46/67 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$46.5); lognormal median ~$44.5, sigma raised from 0.48 to 0.50 because pro forma leverage amplifies price moves, with slightly fatter far-left tail. One-month: centred at $42.0 (from $41.8) with ~16.5% sigma; 15 Oct vote and Q3 print carry no clear directional edge. Extra research was limited to 3 queries; Discovery Alert (flagged low quality) is no longer used for any input.
